correctness.rationale: For every odd prime and exponent, cancellation by translation gives S(A,B)=0 when valuation(A)<valuation(B); reducing and completing the square proves nonvanishing otherwise, with Gauss modulus m^(1/2) established via an exact invertible (x-y,x+y) substitution. These implications force exactly one frequency per first coordinate and the strict-contraction property. The base-p digit equivalence proves all if-and-only-if statements and the complete count, including k=1. The standalone checker uses cyclotomic coefficient cancellation independently on 1518 complete coefficient cases and two direct census cases. Finite tests are evidence, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The fixed quadratic graph is a canonical finite-ring Fourier spectral set with an obvious horizontal basis but a non-obvious moduli-dependent landscape of all frequency partners. The result classifies every partner for all odd primes and positive exponents, explains the digit-tree structure, gives the exact exponential-in-q enumerator and its affine/nonlinear split, and establishes nonlinearity already for p=3,k=2. This structural information is not supplied by a Gauss-sum evaluation alone and is useful for understanding finite-ring spectral geometry.
